Glossary

Every term defined in the book, in alphabetical order. Click a term to jump to where it is first explained.

1/f noise
Fluctuations whose power spectral density scales as 1/f, typical of charge traps in semiconductor devices. (Chapter 4 · Decoherence and noise: T1, T2*, T2 and noise spectra)
AllXY
A calibration sequence of 21 pairs of π and π/2 pulses whose ideal outcomes form a staircase of 0, ½ and 1; deviations reveal specific pulse errors. (Chapter 5 · Gates, measurement and fidelity)
average gate fidelity
Fidelity of a gate averaged over all input states; the standard figure of merit reported for qubit gates. (Chapter 5 · Gates, measurement and fidelity)
Bloch equations
Phenomenological equations for a Bloch vector with longitudinal relaxation time T1 and transverse relaxation time T2. (Chapter 4 · Decoherence and noise: T1, T2*, T2 and noise spectra)
Bloch sphere
A unit sphere on which every pure state of a qubit is a point (polar angle θ, azimuth φ); mixed states lie inside. (Chapter 2 · Two-level systems, states and the Bloch sphere)
Born rule
The rule that the probability of measuring outcome k is the squared magnitude of the amplitude of |k⟩. (Chapter 2 · Two-level systems, states and the Bloch sphere)
Clifford group
The group of 24 single-qubit rotations (11,520 for two qubits) that map Pauli operators to Pauli operators; used in randomised benchmarking. (Chapter 5 · Gates, measurement and fidelity)
coherences
Off-diagonal elements of the density matrix; they carry the phase relationship between basis states. (Chapter 2 · Two-level systems, states and the Bloch sphere)
computational basis
The reference pair of states |0⟩ and |1⟩ in which a qubit is described and measured; for a spin qubit, spin down and spin up along the field. (Chapter 2 · Two-level systems, states and the Bloch sphere)
density matrix
ρ = Σ p_k |ψ_k⟩⟨ψ_k|; describes pure and mixed (statistically uncertain) quantum states. (Chapter 2 · Two-level systems, states and the Bloch sphere)
detuning
The difference between qubit frequency and drive frequency, Δ = ω0 − ω. (Chapter 3 · Driving a qubit: resonance, Rabi oscillations and the rotating frame)
dilution refrigerator
A refrigerator that reaches about 10 mK by mixing helium-3 into helium-4; the standard cryostat for qubit experiments. (Chapter 1 · The big picture: from one electron to a Python notebook)
dynamical decoupling
Sequences of π pulses during free evolution that cancel low-frequency noise and extend coherence. (Chapter 4 · Decoherence and noise: T1, T2*, T2 and noise spectra)
entangled
A multi-qubit state that cannot be written as a product of single-qubit states. (Chapter 2 · Two-level systems, states and the Bloch sphere)
exchange energy
The energy splitting J between singlet and triplet states of two electrons, produced by wavefunction overlap; controlled by gate voltages. (Chapter 2 · Two-level systems, states and the Bloch sphere)
fidelity
A measure (0 to 1) of how close an actual state or operation is to the ideal one. (Chapter 5 · Gates, measurement and fidelity)
filter function
The weighting |Y(f)|² that a pulse sequence applies to the noise spectrum; it shows which noise frequencies cause dephasing. (Chapter 4 · Decoherence and noise: T1, T2*, T2 and noise spectra)
flat-top
A pulse with smooth rising and falling edges and a constant middle section. (Chapter 3 · Driving a qubit: resonance, Rabi oscillations and the rotating frame)
gates
A unitary operation applied to one or more qubits; the quantum analogue of a logic gate. (Chapter 5 · Gates, measurement and fidelity)
global phase
An overall phase factor multiplying a whole state; it has no physical effect. (Chapter 2 · Two-level systems, states and the Bloch sphere)
Hahn echo
A sequence with a π pulse in the middle of free evolution that refocuses slow (quasi-static) noise; measures T2. (Chapter 4 · Decoherence and noise: T1, T2*, T2 and noise spectra)
Larmor precession
The rotation of a spin's Bloch vector around the magnetic field direction at the Larmor frequency. (Chapter 2 · Two-level systems, states and the Bloch sphere)
noise spectroscopy
Using a qubit and pulse sequences with known filter functions to measure the spectrum of its noise environment. (Chapter 4 · Decoherence and noise: T1, T2*, T2 and noise spectra)
Pauli matrices
The three 2×2 matrices σx, σy, σz that, with the identity, form a basis for all single-qubit operators. (Chapter 2 · Two-level systems, states and the Bloch sphere)
power broadening
Broadening of a spectroscopic line when the drive is strong enough to saturate the transition. (Chapter 3 · Driving a qubit: resonance, Rabi oscillations and the rotating frame)
power spectral density
Power spectral density: how the power of a fluctuating quantity is distributed over frequency. (Chapter 4 · Decoherence and noise: T1, T2*, T2 and noise spectra)
probability amplitudes
The complex coefficients multiplying basis states in a superposition; their squared magnitudes give measurement probabilities. (Chapter 2 · Two-level systems, states and the Bloch sphere)
pulse area
The time integral of the Rabi frequency over a pulse; equals the rotation angle on resonance. (Chapter 3 · Driving a qubit: resonance, Rabi oscillations and the rotating frame)
QICK
Quantum Instrumentation Control Kit: open-source firmware and Python software that turns an AMD RFSoC board into a qubit controller. (Chapter 1 · The big picture: from one electron to a Python notebook)
quantum error correction
Encoding logical qubits in many physical qubits so that errors can be detected and corrected faster than they accumulate. (Chapter 5 · Gates, measurement and fidelity)
qubit
A quantum two-level system used to store and process quantum information; the quantum version of a bit. (Chapter 1 · The big picture: from one electron to a Python notebook)
Rabi chevron
2D map of qubit excitation versus drive time and drive frequency; its symmetric pattern locates the resonance and the Rabi frequency. (Chapter 3 · Driving a qubit: resonance, Rabi oscillations and the rotating frame)
Rabi frequency
The angular frequency Ω at which a resonant drive rotates the Bloch vector; f_R = Ω/2π. (Chapter 3 · Driving a qubit: resonance, Rabi oscillations and the rotating frame)
Rabi oscillation
Coherent oscillation of a qubit between |0⟩ and |1⟩ under a resonant drive; its frequency is the Rabi frequency. (Chapter 3 · Driving a qubit: resonance, Rabi oscillations and the rotating frame)
Ramsey experiment
Free-induction sequence X/2 – wait τ – X/2 that measures dephasing and frequency detuning. (Chapter 4 · Decoherence and noise: T1, T2*, T2 and noise spectra)
Randomised benchmarking
Measuring average gate error by applying random gate sequences of increasing length and fitting the decay of the success probability. (Chapter 5 · Gates, measurement and fidelity)
RFSoC
Radio-Frequency System-on-Chip: an AMD (Xilinx) chip combining multi-GHz ADCs and DACs, FPGA fabric and ARM processors on one die. (Chapter 1 · The big picture: from one electron to a Python notebook)
rotating-wave approximation (RWA)
Neglecting terms in the rotating-frame Hamiltonian that oscillate at twice the drive frequency; valid when the Rabi frequency is much smaller than the qubit frequency. (Chapter 3 · Driving a qubit: resonance, Rabi oscillations and the rotating frame)
shot
One complete repetition of an experiment: initialise, manipulate, measure. Results are averaged over many shots. (Chapter 2 · Two-level systems, states and the Bloch sphere)
singlet
The two-spin state (|↑↓⟩ − |↓↑⟩)/√2 with total spin zero. (Chapter 2 · Two-level systems, states and the Bloch sphere)
SPAM
State preparation and measurement errors, which must be separated from gate errors when characterising qubits. (Chapter 5 · Gates, measurement and fidelity)
spectroscopy
Measuring a system's response versus drive frequency to locate its transitions. (Chapter 3 · Driving a qubit: resonance, Rabi oscillations and the rotating frame)
spinQICK
HRL Laboratories' open-source extension of QICK with experiments for gate-defined spin qubits (charge stability, PSB readout, LD and exchange-only control). (Chapter 1 · The big picture: from one electron to a Python notebook)
spin–orbit coupling
Coupling between an electron's motion and its spin, arising from relativistic effects in the crystal's electric fields. (Chapter 4 · Decoherence and noise: T1, T2*, T2 and noise spectra)
state tomography
Reconstructing the full quantum state by measuring along several axes, using rotations before a z measurement. (Chapter 2 · Two-level systems, states and the Bloch sphere)
state vector
A vector in a complex vector space that completely describes a quantum system; written |ψ⟩ in Dirac notation. (Chapter 2 · Two-level systems, states and the Bloch sphere)
superposition
A quantum state that is a weighted combination of basis states, such as a|0⟩ + b|1⟩. (Chapter 1 · The big picture: from one electron to a Python notebook)
T1
The energy relaxation time: the 1/e decay time of the excited-state population. (Chapter 4 · Decoherence and noise: T1, T2*, T2 and noise spectra)
tProcessor
QICK's timed processor: a small custom CPU in the FPGA that schedules pulses and readouts with clock-cycle precision. (Chapter 1 · The big picture: from one electron to a Python notebook)
triplets
The three two-spin states with total spin 1: T+ = |↑↑⟩, T0 = (|↑↓⟩+|↓↑⟩)/√2, T− = |↓↓⟩. (Chapter 2 · Two-level systems, states and the Bloch sphere)
two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG)
Electrons that can move freely in a plane but are confined in the perpendicular direction, typically in a quantum well or at an interface. (Chapter 1 · The big picture: from one electron to a Python notebook)
universal
A set of gates that can approximate any multi-qubit unitary to arbitrary accuracy when combined. (Chapter 5 · Gates, measurement and fidelity)
Zeeman splitting
The energy difference between spin up and spin down in a magnetic field, E_Z = g μB B. (Chapter 2 · Two-level systems, states and the Bloch sphere)
